message.content:
Below are a few common ways to take a screenshot of a webpage that’s currently displayed in Google Chrome using Python. Pick the one that best fits your workflow: | Goal | Tool | Quick‑start code | Notes | |------|------|------------------|-------| | **Capture a page that you *navigate to* with Python** | Selenium WebDriver | ```python
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options

options = Options()
options.add_argument("--headless") # optional – run Chrome without UI
driver = webdriver.Chrome(options=options) # or webdriver.Chrome(executable_path='chromedriver')
driver.get("https://example.com")
driver.save_screenshot("page.png")
driver.quit()
``` | Requires Chrome/Chromium + Chromedriver. Headless mode is handy for CI. | | **Capture a page that you *already opened* in a running Chrome instance** | Chrome DevTools Protocol (via `pychrome` or `pyppeteer`) | ```python
import asyncio
from pyppeteer import launch # or import pychrome

async def main():
browser = await launch(headless=False) # or use launch(args=['--remote-debugging-port=9222'])
page = await browser.newPage()
await page.goto("https://example.com")
await page.screenshot({"path": "page.png"})
await browser.close()

asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(main())
``` | `pyppeteer` is a Python port of Puppeteer; `pychrome` connects to an existing Chrome instance that was started with `--remote-debugging-port`. | | **Take a screenshot of the *visible area* of the Chrome window** | `pyautogui` (or `mss` for higher performance) | ```python
import pyautogui
screen = pyautogui.screenshot() # captures the entire screen
screen.save("full_screen.png")
``` | Captures everything on the screen, not just Chrome. Use `pyautogui.screenshot(region=(x, y, w, h))` to clip to Chrome’s window. | | **Capture only the Chrome window (no other windows)** | `pywinauto` + `Pillow` (Windows only) | ```python
from pywinauto import Desktop
from PIL import ImageGrab

app = Desktop(backend="uia").window(title_re=".*Chrome.*")
rect = app.rectangle()
image = ImageGrab.grab(bbox=(rect.left, rect.top, rect.right, rect.bottom))
image.save("chrome_window.png")
``` | Works on Windows; uses UI Automation to locate the Chrome window. | --- ## 1. Selenium WebDriver ### Install ```bash pip install selenium ``` Download the matching Chromedriver from https://chromedriver.chromium.org/downloads and put it in your PATH or specify `executable_path`. ### Example ```python from selenium import webdriver from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options options = Options() options.add_argument("--headless") # optional options.add_argument("--disable-gpu") # optional driver = webdriver.Chrome(options=options) driver.get("https://www.python.org") driver.save_screenshot("python_org.png") driver.quit() ``` ### Tips * Use `--headless` if you don’t need to see the browser. * For screenshots of the *entire* page (including off‑screen parts), use `driver.execute_script("return document.body.scrollHeight")` to set the viewport height before taking the screenshot. --- ## 2. Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) ### Using `pyppeteer` ```bash pip install pyppeteer ``` ```python import asyncio from pyppeteer import launch async def main(): browser = await launch(headless=False) # or headless=True page = await browser.newPage() await page.goto("https://www.python.org") await page.screenshot({"path": "python_org.png"}) await browser.close() asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(main()) ``` ### Using `pychrome` ```bash pip install pychrome ``` Start Chrome with remote debugging: ```bash chrome.exe --remote-debugging-port=9222 ``` ```python import pychrome browser = pychrome.Browser(url="http://127.0.0.1:9222") tab = browser.list_tab()[0] # first tab tab.start() tab.call_method("Page.navigate", url="https://www.python.org") tab.wait(2) # wait for page load screenshot = tab.call_method("Page.captureScreenshot", format="png") with open("python_org.png", "wb") as f: f.write(screenshot["data"].encode("utf-8")) tab.stop() ``` --- ## 3. Screenshot the Entire Screen (`pyautogui`) ```bash pip install pyautogui pillow ``` ```python import pyautogui # Full screen screenshot = pyautogui.screenshot() screenshot.save("full_screen.png") # Or a specific region (x, y, width, height) region = (100, 200, 800, 600) screenshot = pyautogui.screenshot(region=region) screenshot.save("region.png") ``` > **Note:** `pyautogui` works on Windows, macOS, and Linux (X11). > On Linux you may need to install additional packages (`scrot`, `imagemagick`, etc.). --- ## 4. Capture Only the Chrome Window (`pywinauto`) ```bash pip install pywinauto pillow ``` ```python from pywinauto import Desktop from PIL import ImageGrab app = Desktop(backend="uia").window(title_re=".*Chrome.*") rect = app.rectangle() image = ImageGrab.grab(bbox=(rect.left, rect.top, rect.right, rect.bottom)) image.save("chrome_window.png") ``` > **Platform:** Windows only. --- ## Choosing the Right Approach | Scenario | Recommended Tool | |----------|------------------| | You want to *automatically navigate* to a URL and capture it | Selenium or pyppeteer | | You want to capture a page that’s *already open* in Chrome | pyppeteer (connect to existing instance) or pychrome | | You want to capture the *visible area* of the screen (any app) | pyautogui | | You want to capture only the Chrome window on Windows | pywinauto | Feel free to mix and match. For example, you can use Selenium to open a page, then use `pyautogui` to capture the visible portion if you need a “real‑world” screenshot that includes browser chrome, toolbars, etc.
